messages.content: I want to buy apples, rice, and 12 pack of bottled water from a Walmart near San Jose. Show me the product information and stock availability.

function.name: walmart_purchase
function.description: Retrieve information of items from Walmart including stock availability. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

product_list.description: Items to be purchased listed in an array.

pack_size.description: Size of the product pack if applicable. The size of the array should be equal to product_list. Default is not use it if not specified.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function walmart_purchase with loc "San Jose" or "near San Jose". product_list includes apples, rice, bottled water. pack_size: for bottled water we need 12 pack. So pack_size array length equals product_list length. For apples and rice, no pack size needed; maybe default None? But pack_size optional. We can provide pack_size array with nulls or zeros? The spec says default is not use it if not specified. So we can omit pack_size entirely. But we need to specify 12 pack for bottled water. How to indicate pack size for only one item? The function signature expects pack_size?: number[]. If we provide pack_size array with same length as product_list, we can set pack_size[2] = 12, others maybe 0 or omitted? But spec says default is not use it if not specified. So we could provide pack_size array [null, null, 12]? But type is number[], so null not allowed. Maybe we can provide pack_size array [0,0,12] or [1,1,12] but 0 might mean default. Let's just provide pack_size array [0,0,12]. That indicates no pack size for first two items. Or we can provide pack_size array [null, null, 12] but type mismatch. We'll do [0,0,12].

Thus call function.
